channel.title: FXStreet Forex & Commodities News
channel.description: Real-time Forex News and the latest trading updates. Stay updated on the latest news about currencies and commodities markets.

item.title: Chinese Yuan: Weakness extends after breakout against US Dollar – UOB
item.description: United Overseas Bank’s (UOB) Quek Ser Leang and Lee Sue Ann highlight a sharp USD/CNH spike to 6.8195, now seen consolidating between 6.8030 and 6.8185 on an intraday basis after an overdone rise.

item.title: Fed’s Goolsbee: “Inflation side of mandate is clearly the problem”
item.description: Federal Reserve (Fed) Bank of Chicago President Austan Goolsbee said on Thursday that inflation remains the central challenge for policymakers, warning that price pressure is still moving in the wrong direction despite some signs of improvement in services.

item.title: Banxico leaves interest rates unchanged at 6.50% as expected
item.description: The Bank of Mexico (Banxico) held its main reference rate unchanged at 6.50% in a unanimous decision on Thursday, as expected. Based on its economic projections, Banxico noted that the balance of inflation risks is tilted to the upside.

item.title: USD/CHF Price Forecast: US Dollar retreats below 0.8100 as ‘tweezer top’ forms
item.description: The USD/CHF pair stumbles on Thursday, losing 0.34% during the North American session, as the Greenback’s six-day rally stalls amid falling US Treasury yields, despite a red-hot US Core PCE inflation reading.

item.title: Thailand: BoT steady stance backs fragile growth – DBS
item.description: DBS Group Research economist Chua Han Teng expects the Bank of Thailand (BoT) to keep its policy rate unchanged at 1.00% through 2026, after a second consecutive on-hold decision.

item.title: NZD/USD Price Forecast: RSI flashes oversold as the pair hovers near seven-month lows
item.description: NZD/USD pauses a six-day losing streak on Thursday as the US Dollar (USD) eases following the latest US Personal Consumption Expenditures (PCE) data, which broadly matched market expectations. At the time of writing, the pair trades around 0.5650, virtually unchanged near seven-month lows.

item.title: Gold price rebounds as US Dollar’s rally stalls despite high Core PCE
item.description: Gold (XAU/USD) price recovers on Thursday, up by almost 1% as the Greenback drops despite inflation data suggesting that a ‘higher-for-longer' scenario favors the Federal Reserve (Fed) holding rates steady, despite US President Donald Trump’s desires for lower interest rates.

item.title: Japanese Yen holds near intervention levels as US data supports Fed caution
item.description: The USD/JPY pair trades within the historical intervention zone at 161.80 on Thursday, holding near multi-decade highs as the Japanese Yen remains slightly under pressure amid wide United States-Japan yield differentials.

item.title: WTI rebounds while traders monitor fresh developments in the Strait of Hormuz
item.description: West Texas Intermediate (WTI) crude Oil edges higher on Thursday, snapping a three-day losing streak as short covering lifts prices following the recent selloff to a more than three-month low. At the time of writing, WTI is trading around $71.50, up more than 2% on the day.

item.title: Singapore Dollar: Weakens against US Dollar – UOB
item.description: United Overseas Bank’s (UOB) Quek Ser Leang and Lee Sue Ann keep a constructive view on USD/SGD after the pair briefly touched 1.2991 before closing near 1.2980.

item.title: Euro gains as US Dollar retreats despite firm PCE inflation, German sentiment improves slightly
item.description: The EUR/USD pair elevated slightly near 1.1380 trades with mild gains on Thursday, as the US Dollar (USD) loses momentum despite a fresh batch of United States (US) economic data showing sticky inflation, stronger growth, and resilient labor market conditions.

item.title: Dow Jones Industrial Average prints a record the Nasdaq paid for
item.description: The Dow Jones Industrial Average (DJIA) printed a fresh intraday record near 52,650 on Thursday before easing back toward 52,200, and the temptation is to read that high as a broad vote of confidence. It was nothing of the sort.

item.title: Silver price rebounds after in-line US PCE data eases Dollar support
item.description: Silver (XAG/USD) rebounds on Thursday, trading around $58.65 at the time of writing, up 2.16% on the day.

item.title: Crude Oil: Inventory draws and shorts set stage for rebound – TD Securities
item.description: TD Securities commodity strategists Ryan McKay and Bart Melek note that crude Oil flows through the Strait of Hormuz are gradually normalizing, but around 10–11m b/d of Middle East production remains offline.

item.title: British Pound rebounds as US Dollar bulls fade despite hot Core PCE
item.description: The Pound Sterling (GBP) advances 0.22% against the US Dollar (USD) on Thursday, even though the US economy grew faster than previously reported in Q1, while inflation readings suggest the Federal Reserve (Fed) needs to tighten policy.

item.title: Thai Baht: Long policy hold supports fragile recovery – UOB
item.description: UOB economists Enrico Tanuwidjaja and Sathit Talaengsatya note that the Bank of Thailand (BoT) kept its policy rate at 1.00% and is expected to hold this level through 2027.

item.title: Gold recovers above $4,000 after US PCE data broadly matches expectations
item.description: Gold (XAU/USD) shows signs of stabilization on Thursday as traders digest the latest US Personal Consumption Expenditures (PCE) Price Index, which came broadly in line with market expectations.

item.title: Japanese Yen gains modestly against the US Dollar after US PCE data meets expectations
item.description: USD/JPY trades slightly lower on Thursday as the US Dollar (USD) eases after the latest US Personal Consumption Expenditures (PCE) data broadly matched market expectations. Still, the Japanese Yen (JPY) remains pinned near its 40-year lows. At the time of writing, the pair trades around 161.75.

item.title: Equities: Micron earnings lift Korean equities – MUFG
item.description: MUFG highlights that strong earnings guidance from Micron Technology, a key AI memory supplier, has boosted sentiment in AI and tech stocks.

item.title: Canadian Dollar: BoC balances oil risks and weak growth – TD Securities
item.description: TD Securities strategists note the Bank of Canada’s (BoC) June Summary of Deliberations maintained its recent balancing act between higher Oil price spillover risks and domestic softness.

item.title: Australian Dollar holds steady as US PCE inflation reinforces Fed caution
item.description: The AUD/USD pair trades muted near the 0.6900 area on Thursday, with the Aussie struggling to gain amid a pullback in the US Dollar (USD) as investors digested the latest United States (US) inflation figures and fresh geopolitical risks around the Strait of Hormuz.

item.title: Japanese Yen: Intervention risk near 162 against US Dollar – Scotiabank
item.description: Scotiabank strategists Shaun Osborne and Eric Theoret report USD/JPY is steady ahead of Tokyo Consumer Price Index (CPI), where consensus expects a pickup in both headline and core inflation into the mid-to-upper 1% range.

item.title: Canadian Dollar recovers as Oil prices rebound, US Dollar eases after PCE data
item.description: USD/CAD trades around 1.4205 on Thursday at the time of writing, down 0.21% on the day after recently reaching its highest level in 14 months.

item.title: United States: Long-run growth and China challenge – Commerzbank
item.description: Commerzbank’s Bernd Weidensteiner and Christoph Balz describe the United States as a long‑term growth success, driven by population gains, immigration and productivity, but now facing a serious challenge from China.

item.title: Euro stabilizes near 13-month lows against the US Dollar after in-line US inflation data
item.description: EUR/USD recovers from intraday lows on Thursday as traders digest a heavy batch of US economic data. At the time of writing, the pair trades around 1.1362, staging a rebound from thirteen-month lows reached on Wednesday.

item.title: US Dollar: Rally extends as Fed repricing dominates – ABN AMRO
item.description: ABN AMRO strategist Georgette Boele notes that recent Dollar strength has been driven mainly by a reassessment of the Federal Reserve outlook, with markets now pricing in rate hikes into 2026. She argues this repricing may have gone too far, as ABN AMRO still expects Fed rate cuts around year-end.

item.title: Thai Baht: Negative bias persists under US yield pressure – MUFG
item.description: MUFG’s Lloyd Chan reports broad Asia FX weakness versus the Dollar, with the Thai Baht underperforming. The Bank of Thailand has kept its policy rate at 1% as growth remains low and uneven and credit conditions soft.

item.title: WTI Oil extends decline as Hormuz traffic normalizes, US Iran waiver lifts supply
item.description: West Texas Intermediate (WTI) US Oil trades around $69.30 at the time of writing, down 0.65% on Thursday. The American benchmark Crude is now posting a fourth consecutive day of losses, weighed down by a convergence of supply-side factors reshaping market expectations.

item.title: Gold: Precious metals lead lost-decade playbook – TD Securities
item.description: TD Securities’ Izidor Flajsman highlights that during historical US equity ‘lost decades’, Precious Metals, especially Gold, have delivered strong real returns while broad Commodities were more mixed.

item.title: US Dollar: Long-run erosion and debt risks – Commerzbank
item.description: Commerzbank economists Bernd Weidensteiner and Christoph Balz review 250 years of US economic history, highlighting how persistent inflation has eroded the value of the Dollar and how federal debt has surged back to World War II highs.
